sections.h2: Where is Preston County and what is its terrain like?
sections.html:
Preston County is in the northern part of the state, bordering Pennsylvania to the north and Maryland to the east, and Kingwood is the county seat. The Virginia General Assembly created it on January 19, 1818, from Monongalia County and named it for Governor James Patton Preston. It covers about 651 square miles.

The county lies mostly on the Appalachian Plateau, with elevations from 873 to 3,216 feet. The Cheat River divides it into two sections, and the eastern one is a little larger. The Mason-Dixon Line forms the northern boundary, and part of the Monongahela National Forest, Cathedral State Park and Fairfax Stone State Park lie within it.

Besides Kingwood the county has nine towns: Albright, Brandonville, Bruceton Mills, Masontown, Newburg, Reedsville, Rowlesburg, Terra Alta and Tunnelton. Arthurdale and Aurora are census-designated places. Eight old magisterial districts were merged into five numbered districts in the 1990s.

sections.h2: What does winter mean for a Preston County house?
sections.html:
Preston County is known across the state for hard winters, so a house's cold-weather condition deserves attention. Kingwood's monthly average runs from 28.7 degrees Fahrenheit in January to 70.2 in July, and the county has a warm-summer humid continental climate.

Terra Alta in Preston County holds the state's record monthly snowfall, 104 inches in January 1977. The encyclopedia adds that cold weather sometimes strays into other seasons, and that a frost on June 5, 1859, killed crops in the fields.

  • Keep records of roof, insulation and heating work, since a buyer or lender may ask for them.
  • If the house will sit empty over the winter, arrange for someone to check it after cold snaps.
  • Keep the tax ticket and insurance current while the house is unoccupied.

sections.h2: How did Preston County's history shape its land records?
sections.html:
A fire in 1869 left a gap in the county's paper trail. The encyclopedia says one of the courthouses that replaced the 1820s building was burned by an arsonist in 1869, destroying most of the county records for 1818 to 1869.

That matters to anyone selling an old farm or a parcel with a long chain of title. Deeds from before 1869 may be missing from the courthouse, so a title search can lean on later deeds, surveys and the assessor's tax maps. If a parcel has been in a family for generations, start the paperwork early.

The B&O Railroad arrived in the 1850s and opened markets for timber and coal. Newburg grew as a coal and railroad town, and an explosion at the Orrel Coal Company shaft in January 1886 killed 39 men. The county's population was 3,422 in 1820 and reached a high in the 2020 census.

sections.h2: What does the Preston County economy rely on?
sections.html:
Agriculture, coal and timber remain part of the economy, joined by education, health care, technology, tourism and historic preservation. The encyclopedia also notes the satellite earth station at Etam, which links into an international communications system.

Preston County is part of the Morgantown metropolitan area, and Interstate 68 across the north of the county eases the drive between Monongalia County and Maryland. Other roads include U.S. 50 in the south, U.S. 219, and West Virginia routes 7, 24, 26, 72 and 92. Preston High School at Kingwood serves the whole county, and public school enrollment was 3,872 in 2024-25.

The Buckwheat Festival fills Kingwood on the last weekend of September. It began as a homecoming in 1938, and the encyclopedia says it is also when some of the biggest family reunions bring people back. Median household income in the fact box is $55,755.

sections.h2: Who collects and who assesses property tax in Preston County?
sections.html:
The Sheriff's Tax Office collects and the Preston County Assessor values the property, and both work out of the courthouse at 106 West Main Street in Kingwood.

OfficeDetailsPhone

Because the two sources disagree on the tax office suite, call before you go. The county also links an online tax inquiry and online payment through vendor sites, and the assessor offers tax maps, land records and a sales search through an online portal. Start from the county departments page.

sections.h2: What are the Preston County tax due dates and penalties?
sections.html:
Preston County follows the state calendar. Tickets are issued on or after July 15, and installments are due September 1 and March 1.

  • Take the 2.5 percent discount by paying before September 1 or before March 1.
  • Unpaid first-half tax goes delinquent October 1 and second-half tax April 1.
  • Delinquent tax accrues interest at 9 percent a year.

A parcel that is still delinquent on September 1 lands on the sheriff's second list by September 10. Liens that are not redeemed are certified to the State Auditor on October 31, according to West Virginia Code 11A-3-2. Redemption before certification goes through the sheriff and costs the tax, interest and charges, including $25 for the list and $10 per mailed notice.

sections.h2: Where does Preston County tax revenue go?
sections.html:
Schools take the biggest share, though a smaller one than in Nicholas or Raleigh County. In the State Tax Division's tax year 2024 publication, Preston County levied $23,779,702 across all purposes.

Real estate accounted for $13,001,997 of the total. Class II, meaning property owned, used and occupied by its owner as a residence, was $7,981,104, or about 61 percent. Class III outside municipalities was $3,562,990 and Class IV inside municipalities was $1,457,904. The publication says Class II is taxed at twice the Class I rate and Classes III and IV at four times.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Preston County assessment?
sections.html:
You act during the winter review period, and the county commission hears the case sitting as the board of equalization and review.

West Virginia Code 11-3-24 has the board meet no later than February 1, allows it to adjourn after February 15 and requires it to finish by the last day of February. It can reduce or correct an assessment, and it fixes anything not at 60 percent of true value. An increase needs five days of written notice. If you skip the meeting you give up the correction for that year, other than through the Office of Tax Appeals, and the standard of proof is a preponderance of the evidence.

sections.h2: Can a Preston County owner get the homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Yes, if the owner is 65 or older or certified as permanently and totally disabled and meets the residency test. The exemption covers the first $20,000 of assessed value under West Virginia Code 11-6B-3.

It attaches to the home the owner occupied on July 1 and applies to the following tax year. A transfer by deed or will removes it on the next July 1 unless the new owner qualifies. Heirs should ask the assessor how the change affects the next bill.

sections.h2: What changes when you sell a Preston County house with tax due?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax is paid from proceeds or before closing, and the deed is then recorded with the county clerk. Ask the Sheriff's Tax Office for a payoff on each year, and ask the title company to run the chain of title.

Under West Virginia Code 11-22-2 the transfer tax is $1.10 per $500, retained by the county since July 1, 2025, plus an additional county tax of 55 cents per $500 unless the commission raised it, plus a $20 fee. A $125,000 deed at those base rates is $275, $137.50 and $20, or $432.50. The grantor pays unless the grantee accepts the deed without the tax being paid.

faqs.q: When are Preston County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1. Paying before either date earns a 2.5 percent discount, and unpaid halves become delinquent on October 1 and April 1.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Preston County?
faqs.a: Pay at the Sheriff's Tax Office at 106 West Main Street in Kingwood, phone 304-329-0105, or online through the county's vendor link. Sources list the suite as 101 or 102, so call ahead.

faqs.q: Is there an assessment appeal deadline in Preston County?
faqs.a: The statute has the county commission meet as the board of equalization and review by February 1 and finish by the end of February.

faqs.q: What happens if my Preston County taxes go unpaid?
faqs.a: They accrue 9 percent interest from the delinquency date. A parcel still delinquent on September 1 goes on the sheriff's second list, and the lien can be certified to the State Auditor on October 31.

faqs.q: Do old Preston County deeds exist from before 1869?
faqs.a: Many may not. The encyclopedia says an arson fire in 1869 destroyed most county records from 1818 to 1869, so a title search on an old parcel can depend on later deeds and surveys.
